introduction: Rosalind's place at court depends on the uncle who has banished her father, while Orlando struggles under an elder brother's jealous control. A wrestling match brings them together, and threats at home send them separately toward the Forest of Arden. There, Rosalind's disguise as a young man lets her explore a love she cannot yet openly declare. Among exiled courtiers, shepherds and fools, competing ideas of freedom, affection and good sense meet in conversation, disguise and improvised performances of courtship.

fullSynopsis.text: Orlando resents the neglect of his elder brother Oliver, who has denied him the education and small legacy required under their father's will. Oliver secretly encourages the wrestler Charles to injure him. Instead, Orlando defeats Charles before Duke Frederick and attracts the love of Rosalind, daughter of the Duke whom Frederick has displaced. Frederick dislikes Orlando's father and soon banishes Rosalind because her popularity threatens his daughter Celia's position. Celia refuses to abandon her cousin. They escape with the fool Touchstone, Rosalind dressed as the young man Ganymede and Celia as the poor Aliena.

The fugitives reach Arden, where Rosalind's exiled father, Duke Senior, lives with his followers. Through the shepherd Corin, the cousins arrange to buy a cottage, pasture and sheep. Orlando also flees after the old servant Adam warns that Oliver plans to burn him in his lodging; Adam gives him his savings and accompanies him. When hunger overcomes Adam, Orlando enters Duke Senior's camp with a drawn sword to demand food. The Duke's hospitality disarms him, and he returns with Adam to a welcome strengthened by the Duke's friendship with Orlando's father.

Frederick seizes Oliver's lands and commands him to find Orlando. In the forest, Orlando hangs verses praising Rosalind on the trees. Rosalind discovers their author and approaches him as Ganymede, offering to cure his supposed madness of love. Her method is to let him call the youth Rosalind and practise wooing every day. Orlando agrees without recognizing her, giving Rosalind the freedom to question, tease and test him. Meanwhile, Touchstone debates the virtues of country life with Corin and courts Audrey. Jaques interrupts their proposed wedding by the unreliable Sir Oliver Martext, though Touchstone privately likes the possibility of an easily broken marriage.

Another courtship entangles the disguised Rosalind. Silvius devotedly loves Phoebe, who rejects him; when Ganymede rebukes her cruelty, Phoebe falls for the person she believes is a young man instead. She employs Silvius to deliver her love letter. Rosalind refuses her and urges her toward the faithful shepherd. With Orlando, she stages a mock wedding, makes extravagant predictions about a wife's changeability and punctures romantic claims about dying for love. Once he leaves, she confesses the depth of her own affection to Celia, showing how little her clever performance frees her from longing.

Orlando misses an appointment because, as Oliver reports, he has rescued his sleeping brother from a lioness. Despite Oliver's former hatred, Orlando fights the animal and receives a wound; his kindness converts Oliver into a loving brother. Oliver brings a bloodstained handkerchief to Ganymede, and Rosalind faints, vainly insisting that she was acting. Oliver and Celia fall in love at once. Oliver proposes to give Orlando their father's estate and remain a shepherd. Seeing Orlando weary of imaginary courtship, Rosalind promises that supposed magical knowledge will produce the real Rosalind for marriage on the following day.

Touchstone drives away Audrey's other suitor William. Rosalind binds the lovers to an agreement: Phoebe promises to accept Silvius if she refuses Ganymede. Rosalind then returns in her own clothes beside Celia, accompanied by Hymen, the figure of marriage. Duke Senior and Orlando recognize her, and Phoebe accepts Silvius. Hymen brings together four couples: Rosalind and Orlando, Celia and Oliver, Phoebe and Silvius, and Audrey and Touchstone. Orlando's brother Jaques de Boys reports that Frederick, advancing against the exiles, met a religious man, renounced worldly power and restored the dukedom and confiscated lands. The melancholy Jaques chooses to seek the convert rather than join the dancing; the company celebrates the unions and recovered fortunes.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: Orlando challenges Oliver over his neglected upbringing and withheld patrimony. Oliver conceals his hatred beneath false accusations when Charles the wrestler calls, encouraging Charles to break Orlando's neck. At Frederick's court, Rosalind grieves for her banished father while Celia tries to comfort her. Both women urge Orlando to avoid the dangerous contest, but he wins it and leaves Rosalind and himself mutually captivated. Frederick responds coldly when he learns whose son Orlando is. He then banishes Rosalind, treating her father's identity and the people's sympathy for her as sufficient threats. Celia declares that she will share her cousin's exile and leave her own inheritance behind. They plan to seek Duke Senior in Arden, taking Touchstone with them. Rosalind will travel as the armed youth Ganymede, while Celia becomes Aliena.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: In Arden, Duke Senior finds freedom and instruction in exile, though his followers report Jaques's criticism of their hunting and his sympathy with a wounded deer. Frederick discovers the women's flight and orders Orlando sought. Adam warns Orlando that Oliver means to burn him alive and gives him his savings so they can escape together. Rosalind, Celia and Touchstone arrive exhausted in Arden, hear Silvius lament his love for Phoebe, and arrange with Corin to buy a cottage and flock. As Amiens sings of forest life, Jaques turns pastoral contentment into satire. Hunger overwhelms Adam, and Orlando demands food from Duke Senior at sword point. The Duke answers with kindness. Orlando fetches Adam; Jaques describes the seven ages of human life, and the Duke welcomes his old friend's son.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Frederick confiscates Oliver's property and threatens him with exclusion unless he brings Orlando back. In Arden, Orlando displays his love through poems on trees, provoking Touchstone's parody and Jaques's mockery. Celia reveals the poet's identity to Rosalind, who approaches him as Ganymede. Pretending to offer a cure for love, she invites Orlando to woo her under Rosalind's name; he accepts the daily experiment. Corin's defence of honest rural labour meets Touchstone's courtly sophistry. Touchstone then arranges to marry Audrey through Sir Oliver Martext, but Jaques persuades him toward a proper ceremony. Rosalind becomes distressed when Orlando misses a meeting, then watches Phoebe reject Silvius. Her intervention against Phoebe's pride has an unexpected result: Phoebe falls for Ganymede and recruits the devoted Silvius to carry a letter to her new love.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Rosalind mocks Jaques's cultivated melancholy, then rebukes Orlando for lateness. Their courtship lesson becomes a rehearsal of marriage, with Celia reluctantly speaking the ceremonial words. Rosalind dismisses lovers' claims of fatal heartbreak and predicts the jealous, changeable behaviour of wives; afterward she admits to Celia how deeply she loves Orlando. A hunting song turns deer horns into jokes about marriage. Silvius delivers Phoebe's letter, which Rosalind exposes as an offer of love rather than the angry message he expected. She sends him back with a command that, if Phoebe loves Ganymede, she must love him. Oliver then arrives with Orlando's bloody handkerchief and recounts how Orlando saved him from a lioness, receiving a wound. This mercy has transformed Oliver's hatred into affection. Rosalind faints at the account and cannot convince Oliver that her reaction was merely performed.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Touchstone intimidates Audrey's suitor William into withdrawing. Oliver and Celia have fallen in love and plan to marry; Oliver offers Orlando their father's estate while choosing a shepherd's life. Orlando can no longer be content with imagined wooing, so Rosalind promises to produce his beloved through supposed magic. She also secures Phoebe's agreement to marry Silvius if she refuses Ganymede. At the gathering, Rosalind returns in women's clothes beside Celia, with Hymen presenting the four couples for marriage. Her father and Orlando recognize her, and Phoebe accepts her bargain with Silvius. Jaques de Boys brings news that Frederick has abandoned an armed expedition against the exiles after a religious conversion, restoring the dukedom and their lands. Jaques elects to seek him out, while Duke Senior turns the assembled company toward dancing and celebration.

framing.label: Epilogue
framing.summary: Rosalind turns from the finished action to address the audience, joking about the unusual appearance of a lady as epilogue. She invokes the mutual affection of women and men to win approval for the play, then playfully makes the offer of kisses depend on the speaker being a woman, exposing the actor beneath the character before asking for a kind farewell.
